frames.narration: A customer checks out. Checkout puts an 'order placed' message on the queue instead of calling the email service directly.
The queue stores it durably and checkout carries on immediately. The customer does not wait for the email.
Worker 1 takes the message. While it works on it, the message is hidden from others but not deleted.
Worker 1 crashes before it finishes. It never acknowledges the message.
After a timeout the queue makes the message visible again and gives it to Worker 2. Nothing was lost.
Worker 2 succeeds and acknowledges. Only now is the message deleted. (If Worker 1 had actually sent the email before crashing, it goes out twice: handlers must tolerate duplicates.)
Another message is malformed and fails every time. After a few attempts the queue stops retrying it.
It is moved to the dead-letter queue, where a person can inspect it, while everything else keeps flowing.
